inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026 Total Gross Sales as filed in the FY26 Annual Report (year to 30-Jun-26; DTL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt, results summary; DB core_metrics FY2026 revenue 3,385.279m). Replaces the prior build's results-release estimate of 3,384.8m. Revenue basis is the company's own continuous 'Total Gross Sales' KPI (FY16 983.2m -> FY26 3,385.3m, eleven unbroken years), NOT statutory revenue: the FY24 net/agency recognition change made statutory revenue discontinuous (FY23 808.6m vs FY22 2,192.4m; FY26 statutory 907.0m). All margins below are on gross sales and therefore look thin (adj EBITDA ~2.3%).
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: FY26 AR weighted diluted 155,499,721 (DTL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:3275); shares on issue at 30-Jun-26 155,077,841 (:3270). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Zero buybacks in all eleven years FY16-FY26 (KPI ShareRepurchases = 0 throughout) -- the flat count is a modelling convention funded by the tiny SBC (0.035% of gross sales), not by repurchases; issuance is ~0.1%/yr of LTI shares.
inputs.net_cash_note: Cash anchor is the 31-Dec-2025 (H1 FY26) balance, 125.412m -- the SEASONAL TROUGH -- deliberately NOT the 30-Jun-26 figure of 326.047m from the FY26 AR (DTL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:3336). Data#3 collects from customers in June and pays vendors in July, so June-30 cash is customer/vendor float (June: 405m FY23, 276m FY24, 357m FY25, 326m FY26; Dec: 42m, 117m, 131m, 125m). The eleven-year history now in the DB confirms the pattern every single year (June cash 102-405m vs Dec 7-131m) and shows the Dec trough itself has grown with the business (15m FY16-FY18 -> 125m FY26), i.e. it is the retained-earnings cash plus a structural float minimum. Total equity is only 95.2m, so even the trough exceeds book equity; adding the June figure would count vendor money as shareholders'. total_debt = 0: no borrowings; the only interest-bearing liabilities are AASB 16 lease liabilities (22.672m at 30-Jun-26, :3299), excluded under lease treatment (B). The float interest earned above the anchor is captured once, in equity_bridge. FY26 June cash fell 30.6m y/y mainly because inventory rose 18.4m -> 73.4m (hardware pre-bought ahead of memory-chip price rises) -- a timing item, not a change in the float model.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Normalised FY2026 owner FCF built from the filed P&L because reported FCF is June-30 float timing: adj EBITDA (pre-SBC, pre-lease) 77.599m = reported EBITDA 76.408 + SBC 1.191; less SBC 1.191, lease cash 4.941 (principal 3.772 + interest 1.095 + low-value 0.074), D&A ex-ROU 2.628 (6.567 - 3.939) = EBIT(B) 68.839m; x (1-30%) = 48.19m NOPAT; + D&A 2.628 - normalised capex 3.39 (0.10% of gross sales; FY26 actual 5.042 was a fit-out year) = 47.4m. Cross-check: NPAT 54.522 less after-tax finance income (10.085 x 0.7 = 7.06) = 47.46m. Ties. It deliberately does NOT equal reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income (18.2 - 1.2 - 10.1 = 6.9m): that figure is one year of the float cycle (OCF 23.3m vs 126.3m FY25 vs -86.2m FY24), not a base.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026 as reported: OCF 23.254m less capex 5.042m (payments for property and equipment 4.134m, DTL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:2614, plus 0.908m other investing). Eleven-year reported FCF series is working-capital timing (+3.5, +47.3, +4.8, +8.7, +156.3, -24.6, -26.5, +290.0, -86.8, +124.1, +18.2) and is not used as a base.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY26 finance income 10.085m per the P&L (DTL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:2534; interest received in the cash flow 10.207m, :2597); FY25 10.242m; FY27 guided ~11.1m. Stripped from the flows. Reported EBITDA in the DB already excludes it: EBIT 69.841 + finance income 10.085 - lease interest 1.095 = 78.831 vs PBT 78.794 (37k other finance costs).
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 AR share-based payments expense 1,191 ($'000) (DB core_metrics stock_based_comp FY2026, corrected 2026-09-22 from reserve balance to expense; FY25 1.001m, FY24 1.162m, FY19 0.165m). Equity-award cash taxes nil (KPI EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in every period). Near SBC-zero: 0.035% of gross sales, so house and street bases almost coincide and band_position is not meaningful.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-22T06:10:05Z (16:10 AEST, regular ASX close; Yahoo regularMarketPrice 11.37, 52w 6.42-11.81)
inputs.balance_sheet_note: FY26 Annual Report (filed 2026-09-17) is the latest balance sheet: zero borrowings, lease liabilities 22.672m, cash 326.047m (float peak), inventory 73.4m, equity 95.162m. The cash ANCHOR uses the 31-Dec-25 interim trough (see net_cash_note); everything else is at 30-Jun-26.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows discounted at an AUD-built rate: AU 10y government ~4.4% + beta ~0.95 x 5.5% ERP = ~9.6% cost of equity; no interest-bearing debt so WACC = CoE, rounded to 9.5%. One WACC for all three scenarios -- vendor-incentive, election-cycle and margin risk is charged in the bear flows and weights, not in the discount rate (section 7f). Unchanged from the prior build.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: lease_cost_pct_path charges principal + interest inside EBIT. FY26 cash-flow statement: lease liability payments 3,772 (DTL.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:2629) + interest on lease liabilities 1,095 (:2860) + low-value leases 74 (:3309) = 4,941 ($'000) = 0.146% of gross sales; FY25 was 4,993 = 0.166%. Path set to 0.15% (lease liabilities rose 18.5m -> 22.7m on a new premises lease, so FY27 payments will run a little above FY26's 0.146%). Lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use (6.567 - 3.939 = 2.628m = 0.078%, rounded 0.08%).
inputs.nci_treatment: None required at FY0: no non-controlling interests since FY2021. The DB's FY2016-FY2020 net_income rows are now attributable ('Owners of Data#3 Limited'), so the historical NPAT series is on the same basis as FY26.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing: operating company -- IT reseller/integrator; not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco/distressed shell; no live corporate action). Same route as the prior build of 2026-09-22 (built earlier the same day from the FY26 results release, before the FY26 AR and the FY16-FY18 history were parsed). THIS IS AN UPDATE: anchors refreshed to the filed FY26 AR; driver paths carried over except where stated in reconciliation. REVENUE BASIS: Total Gross Sales throughout (see base_revenue_note). COMPONENT TIE-OUT FY26 (filed): adj EBITDA 2.29% x 3,385.3 = 77.6m; less SBC 1.2, lease 4.9, D&A 2.6 = EBIT(B) 68.8m; x 0.7 = 48.2m; + after-tax float interest 7.1m = 55.3m vs reported NPAT 54.5m (0.8m gap = 0.8pp effective-tax above 30%). HISTORICAL MARGIN BAND on the engine basis (reported EBITDA + SBC, pre-lease; FY16-FY19 pre-AASB16 EBITDA already carries rent so add ~0.3pp): ~2.6% FY16-17, ~2.2% FY18-19, 2.43% FY20, 2.34% FY22, 2.28% FY23, 2.21% FY24, 2.24% FY25, 2.29% FY26 -- eleven years inside 2.2-2.6% with no peak-trough signature, so NOT MID-CYCLED. NPAT (attributable) compounded 13.8m FY16 -> 54.5m FY26 = 14.7%/yr; the FY18 dip (15.4 -> 14.1) is the only down year. Buybacks: none in eleven years; ~90% payout. DATA: H1 net_income rows are now NPAT (H1 FY26 23.171m), the prior build's NPBT flag is resolved. FY2021 EBITDA is NULL in the DB (no FY21 AR in the filing set; row reconstructed from FY22 comparatives) -- not needed for the build; the FY21 margin is interpolated from PBT 36.9m / gross sales 1,955m = 1.89% pre-tax, consistent with neighbours.

equity_bridge.item: Capitalised after-tax interest on the seasonal vendor float above the Dec-25 cash anchor
equity_bridge.note: UNCHANGED from the prior build. Finance income FY26 10.085m / FY27 guided ~11.1m is earned on an average balance of ~225-240m, of which only the 125.4m Dec trough is added as net cash. The ~5-6m/yr pre-tax (~4m post-tax) earned on the float above the anchor is a recurring feature of the collect-then-pay model (FY23 2.8m, FY24 9.9m, FY25 10.2m, FY26 10.1m total finance income). Capitalised at 9.5% with no growth and a ~30% haircut for rate normalisation: 4.1 / 0.095 x 0.7 = ~30m (~$0.19/share). Adding the full June cash (326m) would count vendor money as equity (~+$1.30/share); adding nothing would strip an income stream without its matching asset (section 7d). Would move on: a sustained fall in the Dec trough, or a 150bp+ RBA cut.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: gross_sales_5yr_cagr_faded: FY21-26 gross sales CAGR 11.6% (10yr 13.2%) faded to 8% for FY27 -- Gartner's 8.9% CY2026 Australian IT-spend forecast, FY26's +12.7% flattered by the Windows 11 device refresh, and the memory-chip shortage constraining hardware availability through CY2026. Unchanged from the prior build; the FY28-FY31 fade is now 0.5pp/yr gentler (see reconciliation).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.1% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 16.3% (32% divergence, just over the 30% flag). Cause is the ~90% dividend payout (FY26 90.3%), which caps book-value compounding; equity CAGR is not the growth anchor here. Over ten years equity compounded 8.9% vs EPS 14.6% for the same reason. Owner-FCF CAGR (10.6% / 13.8%) sits below EPS CAGR over 3 years because after-tax float interest grew from ~0.2m (FY22) to ~7m (FY24-26) as rates rose -- that part of EPS growth is stripped from owner FCF.
historical_growth.notes: All series from the corrected 11-year DB (AUD millions, attributable NPAT, EPS in dollars). Revenue = Total Gross Sales: 3yr FY23 2,560.7 -> FY26 3,385.3; 5yr FY21 1,955.2; 10yr FY16 983.2. EPS: 3yr FY23 $0.2396 -> FY26 $0.3516; 5yr FY21 $0.1651; 10yr FY16 $0.0898. Equity: 3yr FY23 68.3 -> FY26 95.2; 5yr FY21 56.3; 10yr FY16 40.6. Owner FCF = NPAT less after-tax finance income (D&A ex-ROU ~= normalised capex): 3yr FY23 35.1 -> FY26 47.5; 5yr FY21 24.9; 10yr FY16 ~13.1 (FY16 interest ~1.0m assumed, first disclosed FY18 1.044m). Attributable NPAT 13.83 -> 54.52 over ten years with one down year (FY18). Reported FCF CAGRs are meaningless (series is +3.5, +47.3, +4.8, +8.7, +156.3, -24.6, -26.5, +290.0, -86.8, +124.1, +18.2).

base.narrative: FY27 gross sales +8% (Gartner 8.9% AU IT spend; Windows 11 refresh fading; memory-chip shortage), fading 0.5pp/yr to 6% by FY31 -- the five-year DTA sole-panel Microsoft VSA (largest contract in company history, held since 2008) and the renewed NSW panel underwrite the FY27-FY31 public-sector base -- then 5% to 3% by FY36. Adj EBITDA margin dips from FY26's 2.29% to 2.18% in FY27 (staff costs +10%, ~$2m AI-practice/Sovereign-SOC investment drag, Microsoft CSP 'Core' incentive removal from Oct-26 only partly fee-substituted, ICR guided flat at 77.5%) then recovers to 2.28% as the reset annualises and Services/managed-security mix rises -- inside the 2.2-2.6% band of every year FY16-FY26. Cash tax 30% statutory (FY26 effective 30.8%). WC capture 0: the Dec-trough cash was flat FY25->FY26 despite 12.7% sales growth, so no float growth is credited. Capex 0.10% of gross sales (11-yr average 2.9m; FY26 5.0m fit-out year) vs D&A ex-ROU 0.08%. Terminal 2.5% at 9.5% WACC (Gordon ~14.6x FCF, inside the 18x cap).

bull.narrative: FY21-26 gross-sales CAGR (11.6%) persists for three years on GenAI/agentic-AI, sovereign security and Azure demand plus a public-sector rebound anchored by the DTA VSA and Brisbane 2032 build-out; Software GP returns to low-double-digit growth as fee-based advisory fully substitutes lost Microsoft rebates; Services 'much better' and MXDR/Sovereign SOC lift mix so ICR falls from 77.5% toward 73%, taking adj EBITDA to 2.48% of gross sales (back to the FY16-FY17 level, above the FY20 2.43% post-AASB16 peak). Recurring/annuity mix (70%) grows the vendor float, credited at 1% of the sales increase. Growth and margin paths unchanged from the prior build.

bear.narrative: Microsoft's FY27 CSP overhaul (removal of 'Core' incentives on M365/D365 for indirect resellers, 5% legacy-product margin cut from Oct-26) is NOT offset by fee substitution and is followed by further program cuts, compressing Software GP in the ~68%-of-sales segment; an IT-spend slowdown, the memory-chip shortage and state/federal election delays hold gross sales growth to 1-3%; the Project Services (-15.3% FY26) and People Solutions (-8.7%) turnarounds stall; price competition in a 'highly competitive and disaggregated' market and the staff-cost step-up push adj EBITDA down to 1.85% of gross sales -- below the FY18-FY19 trough of ~2.2% on this basis -- before a partial recovery to 1.95%. Vendors tighten payment terms so growth consumes a little cash (WC capture -1%). Still profitable throughout -- no going-concern element -- and the terminal value stays well off the zero floor. Growth and margin paths unchanged from the prior build.

scenario_narratives.base: Data#3 keeps compounding as Australia's top-tier Microsoft/Cisco/HP partner: gross sales grow 8% fading to 3%, adj EBITDA margin dips in FY27 on the Microsoft CSP reset and the AI/SOC investment step-up, then recovers to ~2.28% of gross sales -- the lower-middle of its eleven-year 2.2-2.6% band. Near-100% conversion of NOPAT to owner FCF (capex ~= D&A) and a ~90% payout make this a dividend compounder; the value is a stream of ~$47m growing at mid-single digits, plus the Dec-trough cash and the capitalised float interest. The five-year DTA sole-panel Microsoft VSA is why the FY28-FY31 fade is gentler than in the first build.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI, sovereign-security and cloud demand plus a public-sector rebound sustain the 11.6% five-year gross-sales CAGR for three more years, Services mix and AI-driven internal efficiency push ICR from 77.5% toward 73% and adj EBITDA to ~2.5% of gross sales, and the growing annuity book adds float. Requires both above-market growth AND margin expansion while the largest vendor is cutting channel incentives.
scenario_narratives.bear: The vendor that sets ~68% of gross sales' economics keeps re-cutting incentives faster than Data#3 can replace them with fees; growth stalls at 1-3% through an IT-spend lull and election cycles; thin 9% gross margin (already down from 9.6%) leaves nowhere to absorb the staff-cost step-up, and EBITDA/gross sales falls below the eleven-year floor to ~1.85%. The business remains profitable and debt-free -- the downside is a de-rating of a 32x P/E reseller, not solvency.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25 (off the 15/50/35 default). Bear at 25%: Microsoft's channel economics are a single-counterparty dependency in the segment that is ~68% of gross sales, and the risk is not hypothetical -- the Dec-2024 EA incentive cut compressed Software GM from 3.6% to 3.4% in FY26 and a second overhaul is scheduled for Oct-2026; the DTA VSA deepens rather than dilutes that dependency. Bull at 25%: it needs above-market growth AND ~20bp of margin expansion at the same time as the vendor is squeezing, i.e. two independent things going right. Base 50%: the eleven-year record of 2.2-2.6% EBITDA/gross sales and 14-15% NPAT compounding with one down year is the most likely path. Would move on: a Microsoft incentive change materially worse than the Oct-26 package (bear up), or two consecutive halves of Software GP growth above 10% post-reset (bull up).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the owner cash flow of a capital-light, debt-free IT reseller/integrator on its own continuous gross-sales basis, with the customer/vendor float treated as float (Dec-trough cash plus capitalised float interest) rather than as a June-30 cash pile, leases charged once inside EBIT, SBC (immaterial) expensed with a flat share count, and vendor-incentive risk carried in the bear flows and weights rather than in a scenario-specific WACC. The finding is that at ~32x FY26 EPS the market is pricing DTL for perpetual double-digit growth that even the corrected eleven-year record (13% sales, 15% NPAT) does not make the base case for a reseller with 2.3% EBITDA margins.
key_risks_to_valuation: Microsoft (and other vendor) incentive-program changes: a 20bp move in EBITDA/gross sales is ~10% of EBIT on a 2.3% margin business
Revenue basis: all sales multiples are on Total Gross Sales (3.7x the statutory figure); mixing bases in any sanity check will look either absurdly cheap or absurdly expensive
Float accounting: June-30 cash of $326m is largely vendor money -- a model that adds it as net cash overstates value by ~$1.30/share; the Dec-trough anchor and 30m bridge are the deliberate middle
The base case assumes growth fades to 3% by FY36; the eleven-year record is 13% -- if Data#3 keeps taking share at the ten-year rate the bull case is the base
Interest-rate sensitivity of the ~$10-11m float income (stripped from flows, partly captured in the bridge) -- a 150bp RBA cut removes ~$3.5m pre-tax
Public-sector concentration and election-cycle timing (FY25 Queensland/federal delays) can shift a year's growth between periods
